identity.title: ReQAT: Achieving Full-Precision Reasoning Accuracy with 4-bit Floating-Point Quantization-Aware Training

problem.claim: Deploying large reasoning models efficiently while preserving reasoning accuracy under 4-bit floating-point quantization.

gap.claim: Fully quantized W4A4KV4 deployment causes severe reasoning degradation, and existing PTQ and QAT reportedly fail to recover it.

contributions.claim: ReQAT, a reasoning-centric FP4 quantization-aware training framework combining Trace-Aligned QAT, Selective Entropy Minimization, and Q-FIT initialization with RoPE-consistent KV-cache calibration.
An identified failure pattern: FP4 errors concentrate on low-entropy symbolic decisions, where sampling errors can cascade through reasoning traces.
The authors report accuracy recovery beyond BF16 fine-tuning under the same training budget, alongside substantial hardware-specific throughput gains.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors present ReQAT as a reasoning-centric FP4 training framework centered on low-entropy decision preservation and jointly calibrated KV-cache transformations.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that ReQAT recovers and surpasses BF16 fine-tuning accuracy under the same training budget.
The authors report up to 3.9× throughput speedup on NVIDIA DGX Spark and 3.1× on B200.

narrative_sequence.summary: Large reasoning models incur costly full-precision inference and growing KV-cache footprints.
Microscaled FP4 supports efficient deployment, but fully quantizing weights, activations, and KV caches severely degrades reasoning, beyond reported recovery by existing PTQ and QAT.
The authors attribute concentrated FP4 failures to noisy low-entropy symbolic commitments whose sampling errors cascade through reasoning traces.
ReQAT addresses this with trace-aligned updates, entropy minimization at critical positions, and quantization-friendly KV-cache-aware initialization.
The authors report exceeding BF16 fine-tuning accuracy and achieving hardware-dependent throughput speedups.

source_observation.claim: The abstract links quantization failures to low-entropy symbolic decisions and then aligns training updates and confidence reinforcement with those positions.

lessons.interpretation: Error localization can motivate targeted optimization objectives instead of uniform treatment of all tokens.
lessons.application: For another sequence-model compression problem, identify decision positions associated with downstream error cascades and weight training or calibration toward them.
lessons.exception: This move may be unsuitable when failure localization is unverified, unavailable, or when errors do not propagate through identifiable decision points.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify datasets, model sizes, accuracy values, baselines beyond BF16 fine-tuning, or statistical variability.
The reported speedups are hardware-specific; runtime settings and comparison implementations are not given.
The causal account connecting low-entropy quantization noise to cascading errors is presented but not experimentally detailed in the abstract.
